summary.headline: Before any AI agent goes live, build these four things: an eval harness, versioned config, a dev/test/prod path, and an ops runbook.
summary.narrative: Most teams can launch an agent faster than they can prove it works or roll it back. This framework closes that gap. Stand up the eval harness first — it's the gate every config change and promotion depends on. This is a framework you implement; nothing here is deployed for you.

findings.title: Eval harness: historical-case test sets run cold-start, accumulated-context, and as regression
findings.what_we_found: There is no repeatable way to prove the agent produces the right outcome on known cases, and no test that re-runs when the config changes.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Without an eval harness you ship on vibes — you can't tell whether a prompt tweak improved or silently broke the agent, and you discover regressions in production from real customers.
the_fix: Build a test set from real historical cases: each case's inputs paired with its known-good outcome.
Run the set cold-start (no prior context) to measure baseline reasoning.
Run the same set with accumulated production-like context to confirm the agent doesn't drift or over-rely on history.
Wire the full set as a regression suite that re-runs on every config change; a change may not ship if it regresses any case.
Track pass rate per run and store results alongside the config version that produced them.
findings.evidence: No existing eval test set or regression gate for the planned case-triage agent.

findings.title: Versioned, rollback-able configuration discipline
findings.what_we_found: Prompts, tool definitions, model choice, and guardrails would be edited in place with no version history and no clean way to revert.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: If you can't see what changed or roll back atomically, a bad change stays live until someone reconstructs the previous config by hand — turning a small mistake into a prolonged incident.
the_fix: Put every agent artifact (prompts, tool defs, model selection, guardrails) under version control with a version tag.
Make any deployed version atomically rollback-able — reverting is a single tagged action, not a manual rebuild.
Forbid untracked, hand-edited production config; all changes flow through version control.
Record which config version is live in each environment at all times.
findings.evidence: No version control or rollback path defined for agent configuration.

findings.title: Dev / test / prod model with eval-gated promotion
findings.what_we_found: Changes would be made directly against the production agent, with no isolated place to validate them first.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Editing prod directly means every experiment is a live experiment on real customers, and there is no gate that stops a bad change from reaching them.
the_fix: Promote to test and run the full eval harness there.
Promote to prod only after a clean regression run; never edit prod directly.
Record the config version and eval result for every promotion.
findings.evidence: No environment separation between where changes are made and where customers are served.

findings.title: Live-fleet ops runbook: monitoring, tuning, incident response, lifecycle
findings.what_we_found: There is no defined way to watch a live agent, adjust it safely, respond when it misbehaves, or retire it at end of life.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: An unmonitored agent degrades silently — quality slips, escalations climb, cost drifts — and with no incident playbook the first sign of trouble is a customer complaint.
the_fix: Monitoring: watch output quality, escalation/handoff rate, latency, and cost; alert on threshold breaches.
Tuning: define how and when config is adjusted, always via the dev→test→prod path and the eval gate.
Incident response: define detection signals, containment (pause/disable the agent), and atomic rollback to the last good version.
Lifecycle: version, deprecate, and retire agents on a schedule; decommission identities and audit access on retirement.
findings.evidence: No production monitoring, tuning policy, incident playbook, or lifecycle plan for live agents.
